q: I've made sure I have an aisle seat so I can get up and stretch. I've bought a little travel-size lumbar support pillow. But it's also the airport at both ends of the journey that's worrying me, especially standing up to queue.
cx: UK woman at 20 weeks with hip pain preparing for a four-hour holiday flight.

q: I would feel bad officially requesting assisted travel, as I don't need a wheelchair and I'm not even very visibly pregnant, so jumping the queue would feel very cheeky!
cx: Same woman reluctant to ask for help because she doesn't look pregnant yet.

q:
And I hate it when people say “awww honey it’s gonna get worse”   
YOU THINK???
cx: At 22 weeks with constant heartburn, on the comment she keeps hearing.

q: I even went to the hospital who made sure my baby was okay and then just sent me home with muscle relaxers (🙄 I feel like my pain doesn’t matter as long as the baby is okay)
cx: At 31 weeks, new severe pelvic pain; she feels the hospital cared only about the baby.

q: And my work denied me taking maternity leave early so I HAVE to work until I give birth.
cx: Same woman, barely able to walk, refused early leave.

q: besides this pregnancy I haven’t been unemployed since I turned 16 and assumed I’d work forever. Now I’ve been presented an option to choose a different direction, I feel almost guilty to take it.
cx: At 16 weeks, a first-timer who left a new job over severe sickness weighs staying home for good.

q: Everything I've read says that the second trimester is when woman feel better but that has not been my experience at all.
cx: An easy first trimester followed by headaches, hip pain, heat sickness and exhaustion in the second.

q: idk if it's because I have to be up before the sun to get to work, but I am SO TIRED now. This past week I conked out at 6:45 because I just couldn't keep my eyes open any longer.
cx: Same woman on second-trimester tiredness.

q: I wake up feeling MISERABLE, my hands are shaking, my throat is all clogged, I feel like my heart is closed in a box (idk if that makes sense), I feel like crying
cx: At 7 weeks she describes waking from naps.

q: Hit the 15 week mark and tomorrow my husband and I are going to share the news with both of our families but I am terrified of stepping out of our secret “we are pregnant” bubble!
cx: At 15 weeks, the night before telling both families.

q: We know this will open the floodgates of questions and opinions. My MIL was a labor and delivery nurse so I just know we will be in for the many questions to roll in!
cx: Same woman bracing for questions once families know.

q: We actually had a shirt made up for my 4 year old niece to put on that says “my aunt has my best friend in the oven” so we don’t have to say it
cx: Same woman's plan to announce without having to say it.

q: I’m just frustrated that we’ll be missing out on family support (again) because this cousin’s share of the family gets more attention, while I’m on the broken divorced side AND have no family on my husband’s side.
cx: At 7 weeks, still secret, while a favoured cousin announces at 12 weeks.

q: I asked her lots about her first trimester because 1. I do care as I know it’s a lonely experience but also because 2. I was taking notes since I’m right behind her
cx: Same woman secretly learning from the cousin five weeks ahead.

q: I was sick two days last year and someone texted me that they had money on morning sickness, this year coming back from summer someone told me they were hoping I’d come back with a bump.
cx: Same woman on coworkers who have been waiting for her pregnancy.

q: My husband and I keep saying the pregnancy/baby will show us who the real ones are overall.
cx: Same woman; most of their friends and family are child-free.

q: So all I've been thinking about is how I'll be recovering from childbirth (likely a C Section), adjusting to 2 kids, and my toddler will be bringing home new illnesses all at the same time.
cx: Due with baby two next week as her 3-year-old starts preschool.

q: I'm just worried about all these changes happening for my daughter and all the horror stories of how sick she will get is also stressing me out.
cx: Same mother on what she has heard about preschool illness.

q: my husband and I are starting to build some decision trees for when baby is here (I know that making a plan is a fool's errand, so "decision trees" it is lol).
cx: A first-timer and her husband planning how they'll handle newborn sleep.

q: I've been reading about the Possums sleep program and it feels like a really good fit for us. It basically describes our approach to sleep even as no-child adults.
cx: Same woman on the sleep programme she has been reading before the birth.

q: One option is to do shifts, but breastfeeding might complicate that and pumping sounds like a nightmare that I want to avoid doing too much of if I can. Also, my husband gets a lot of parental leave--4 months. More than me even.
cx: Same woman weighing night shifts with her husband's long leave.

q: Is it a totally crazy idea to spend the first couple of months pretending we don't have circadian rhythms and truly "sleeping when the baby sleeps"?
cx: Same woman asking parents whether her plan is realistic.

q: I’ve been applying the stretch mark oil and lotions but it doesn’t seem to really be helping much.
cx: At 27 weeks, stretch marks spreading on thighs, hips and bottom.

q: Tonight I looked in the mirror and just cried. With having 13 weeks to go I’m scared that I will have SO many stretch marks by the end and look horrible.
cx: Same woman, previously body-confident.

q: My mom has made comments about how hers weren’t nearly this bad when I showed her and that made me feel worse about it all.
cx: Same woman on her mother's reaction to the stretch marks.

q: So now i’m due in 4 weeks, scheduled for a c-section and i’ll be lucky if I can afford to take 4-6 weeks off due to their own massive fuck up.
cx: An HR filing error meant her short-term disability cover never started; she learned this when planning leave.

q: the insurance company couldn’t backdate it far enough to where my pregnancy wouldn’t be considered a pre-existing condition
cx: Same woman on why the insurer refused to fix it.

q: My parents leave and I’m exhausted doing all things baby alone will recovering.
cx: Nine days after a planned section with her second, her toddler and husband quarantined away from her.

q: Wednesday my toddler finally finished antibiotics and is good to mingle which is good because I’m a wreck without him.
cx: Same mother on missing her toddler in the first week home.

q: I am very very scared, but taking it day by day. I think I’m just very overwhelmed and trying to wrap my head around all of this. It feels insane 😂
cx: A day after a positive test that came sooner than she expected.

q: I was scouring Reddit threads looking for others mentioning cramping and I never really found anything so this makes me feel a lot better.
cx: At about 5 weeks, searching for others with the same early symptom.

q: I still look like I’m about 4-5 months pregnant and I’m scared I’m never going to have a flat stomach again.
cx: A first-time mother four weeks after an unplanned section.

q: I dug out my pre-pregnancy clothes today and tried on some jeans. I couldn’t even get them past my thighs and I just feel sad.
cx: Same mother trying on her old jeans.

q: I don’t know anything about epidurals besides they go in your back/spine. Too scared to look into it.
cx: Due in spring, panicking late at night about the epidural needle.

q: I don’t want to know how big or long it is or anything else. I just would like someone to clear that up for me..
cx: Same woman wants one fact, not the full explanation.

q: I’m petrified of needles. Pain I’m not scared of it’s literally the thought of a needle in my skin- Arm, Tattoos, EPIDURAL?? terrifying..
cx: Same woman: the needle, not the pain, is the fear.

q: The other day my husband was prepping some stuff for the hospital bag and she was like "she's got you cleaning stuff now?" And he was like "no I've got myself cleaning stuff, this is my baby too!"
cx: At 9 months, her mother needles her about a husband who reads pregnancy books and helps.

q: things like read books about pregnancy and postpartum care and make me meals and massage my swollen feet (the bar is in hell right?)
cx: Same woman on what her husband does.
